ideas.name: True or false
ideas.kid: Every sentence is true or false, pick one

ideas.name: If then
ideas.kid: If this, then that. Check the if first

ideas.name: Cross it off
ideas.kid: Cross off what it cannot be

ideas.name: Find the rule
ideas.kid: Look at what changes from one to the next

ideas.name: Break the pattern
ideas.kid: Try to make the rule fail

ideas.name: Common bottom
ideas.kid: Make the bottoms the same before you add

ideas.name: Same slice
ideas.kid: Cut both into the same size slices

ideas.name: Of means times
ideas.kid: Of means times

ideas.name: Place value shift
ideas.kid: Moving the point moves every digit

ideas.name: Flip and multiply
ideas.kid: Divide by a fraction, flip it and multiply

ideas.name: Percent is per hundred
ideas.kid: Percent means out of one hundred

ideas.name: Same or different
ideas.kid: Sort into two piles, what stays the same?

ideas.name: More socks than drawers
ideas.kid: More socks than drawers, so two share

ideas.name: What stays the same
ideas.kid: Find something that never changes

ideas.name: Two way check
ideas.kid: Prove it works, then prove nothing else does

ideas.name: Halve the search
ideas.kid: Guess the middle, throw half away

ideas.name: Compare and swap
ideas.kid: Compare two, swap if wrong, repeat

ideas.name: Count the steps
ideas.kid: Count moves, not distance

ideas.name: Unit price
ideas.kid: Price for one, then compare

ideas.name: Number line
ideas.kid: Put it on the line, left is less

ideas.name: Keep the balance
ideas.kid: Do the same to both sides

ideas.name: Work backwards
ideas.kid: Start at the end and undo

ideas.name: Print what it sees
ideas.kid: Show the number before you trust it

ideas.name: Look at the training
ideas.kid: A model only knows what you showed it

ideas.name: Guess and round
ideas.kid: Estimate with easy numbers first

ideas.name: Do the inside first
ideas.kid: Do the inside part first, then the rest

ideas.name: Fold it in your head
ideas.kid: Fold it in your head, one square at a time

ideas.name: Turn it in your head
ideas.kid: Turn it in your head and check each corner

ideas.name: Count the hidden ones
ideas.kid: Count the hidden ones too, layer by layer

ideas.name: Dots and lines
ideas.kid: Draw the connections as dots and lines first

ideas.name: Count the lines
ideas.kid: Count how many lines touch one dot

ideas.name: Color the map
ideas.kid: Give connected dots different colors, using as few as you can

ideas.name: Domino idea
ideas.kid: If the first one falls, and each one knocks over the next, they all fall

ideas.name: The gate
ideas.kid: A switch question; AND needs both, OR is happy with either

ideas.name: Exponents fast forward
ideas.kid: An exponent is multiplication's fast forward button

ideas.name: The winning position
ideas.kid: A spot from which correct play always wins; find them by working backwards

ideas.name: Test it or trust it
ideas.kid: Some claims you can check yourself; know which kind you are holding

ideas.name: Two symbols are enough
ideas.kid: With just on and off you can write any number there is

ideas.name: Numbers wear costumes
ideas.kid: Pixels and sounds are numbers dressed up

ideas.name: Copycat pairing
ideas.kid: Answer their move with its twin to keep the game balanced

ideas.name: Money snowball
ideas.kid: Money earning money earns more money

ideas.name: XOR, the difference detector
ideas.kid: On exactly when the two inputs disagree

ideas.name: Machines can add
ideas.kid: Wire the right questions together and the circuit adds by itself

ideas.name: Domino proof
ideas.kid: Prove the first step, prove each step knocks over the next, and the whole line falls

ideas.name: Sketch, then ink
ideas.kid: A breadboard is a sketch, solder is ink; make it permanent only once you understand it

ideas.name: Primes are atoms
ideas.kid: Every number is built from primes in exactly one way

ideas.name: The letter is a box
ideas.kid: A letter in math is a labeled box holding a number you do not know yet

ideas.name: The threshold
ideas.kid: One number that splits two worlds, like bright and dim or near and far

ideas.name: Data teaches the machine
ideas.kid: The smart part came from the examples, so bad examples make a bad machine

ideas.name: Gcd and lcm
ideas.kid: The biggest shared piece and the first shared meeting

ideas.name: Job, facts, limits
ideas.kid: Tell the machine the job, the facts and the limits, then check what comes back

ideas.name: Squeeze the list
ideas.kid: Mean, median and range each squeeze a whole list into one honest number

ideas.name: Sense, think, act
ideas.kid: A robot runs a loop; read the world, decide, do, repeat

ideas.name: Robot moods
ideas.kid: A machine can remember which mood it is in and act differently in each

ideas.name: Clock math
ideas.kid: Keep only the remainder and patterns start to loop

ideas.name: Binary balance
ideas.kid: Write each pile in binary and pair the powers; a balanced position is a doomed one

ideas.name: Choices multiply
ideas.kid: When choices stack, multiply the ways

ideas.name: Pay yourself first
ideas.kid: Save your slice before the spending starts

ideas.name: Fit the cap
ideas.kid: A real plan fits a real number; the budget decides, not the wish

ideas.name: Corners on a line
ideas.kid: Tear a shape's corners off and lay them together: a straight line holds 180 degrees and a full turn holds 360

ideas.name: Area in pieces
ideas.kid: An odd shape is easy rectangles in disguise; chop it, count the pieces, add

ideas.name: Count the ways
ideas.kid: Chance is the ways you want, counted against all the ways there are

ideas.name: The long run
ideas.kid: Chance is wobbly in ten tries and calm in a thousand

ideas.name: Next-word guessing
ideas.kid: A chatbot plays predict-the-next-word using everything it has read

ideas.name: The square on the side
ideas.kid: The two small squares exactly fill the big one

ideas.name: Nearest neighbour
ideas.kid: To label a mystery point, ask which known point it sits closest to

ideas.name: Read the input
ideas.kid: A program that listens before it speaks; the question comes in on lines, the answer goes out

ideas.name: Save point
ideas.kid: A commit is a save point on the trail; you can always walk back to a camp you already reached

ideas.name: The timer is the referee
ideas.kid: Both sides share one clock; finishing on time is a skill, not a punishment

ideas.name: Two walks, one day
ideas.kid: When one path is travelled twice, picture both journeys on the same day; heading opposite ways, they have to pass

ideas.name: Loop over the herd
ideas.kid: Visit each one once, keep a running answer

ideas.name: Simulate it
ideas.kid: Act the story out step by step, then read how it ends

ideas.name: Fast forward rules
ideas.kid: Write the multiplication out long and the rule falls out

ideas.name: Split the rectangle
ideas.kid: A number outside a bracket has to reach every part inside it; cut the rectangle at the plus sign and both pieces still count

ideas.name: A README for a human
ideas.kid: Write it for the next person, not for the machine; the next person is usually future you

ideas.name: Ship it
ideas.kid: Work that lives only on your laptop is a rehearsal; shipped where other people can reach it, it becomes real

ideas.name: Flow the argument
ideas.kid: Notes in columns, so you answer what was actually said instead of what you wished they had said

ideas.name: Story math
ideas.kid: Adding and taking away are things that happen in a story: act the story out, then count what is true at the end.

ideas.name: Casework
ideas.kid: Split the problem into every kind of case, solve each small one, add them up; the craft is letting no case hide

ideas.name: The mystery number in both pans
ideas.kid: When the mystery number sits in both pans, take the same amount off each until one pan is clean

ideas.name: Fixed or per unit
ideas.kid: Some costs happen once and some happen every single time; keep them in different pockets

ideas.name: Break-even
ideas.kid: The count where the money coming in has finally caught the money going out; before it every sale is still climbing, after it is profit

ideas.name: Assume the opposite
ideas.kid: Assume the opposite is true and chase it until it breaks; the crash is the proof

ideas.name: Try them all
ideas.kid: When the choices are few enough, test every single one and keep the best

ideas.name: Count the steps first
ideas.kid: Before you try them all, work out how many tries that is; a computer is fast, not infinite

ideas.name: Two ratios in balance
ideas.kid: Two ratios set equal make an equation, so solve it with legal moves on both pans, never with a chant you were handed

ideas.name: Paint the board
ideas.kid: Colour the squares and the impossible shows itself, because counting squares alone cannot see it

ideas.name: Collapse to your best
ideas.kid: In the last speech, pick the one argument you are actually winning and spend the whole minute there

ideas.name: Profit is what remains
ideas.kid: Money taken in is not money made; profit is what is left after every cost is paid

ideas.name: Margin as a percent
ideas.kid: Profit compared with the price, so a lemonade stand and a supermarket can be judged on the same scale

ideas.name: The loan comes first
ideas.kid: Borrowed money is paid back before any profit is counted

ideas.name: Opportunity cost
ideas.kid: Every yes is a quiet no to something else; a choice costs you the best thing you gave up

ideas.name: The number that only falls
ideas.kid: Find a number that moves one way only, toward a wall it cannot pass, and the thing has to stop

ideas.name: Root undoes square
ideas.kid: The square root asks which number, multiplied by itself, made this one

ideas.name: Match them up
ideas.kid: Pair two collections one for one and counting either one has counted both

ideas.name: Count the opposite
ideas.kid: Count the ones you do not want and take them off the whole; sometimes the opposite is the smaller job

ideas.name: Every pair counted twice
ideas.kid: Count outwards from everybody and each pair turns up twice, once from each end, so halve it

ideas.name: The compiler reads first
ideas.kid: C++ reads the whole file and translates it before it runs a single line

ideas.name: An error before the run
ideas.kid: A compile error is a bug caught before it could ever happen, and the strictest reader turns out to be the kindest

ideas.name: Slope is the per
ideas.kid: Every straight line has a per: how much it climbs for one single step across

ideas.name: The law of a line
ideas.kid: A starting amount plus the same step over and over, and knowing both means knowing the whole line

ideas.name: Say why they won
ideas.kid: A judge's decision is itself an argument: name the clash, weigh it, then conclude

ideas.name: Types are promises
ideas.kid: Every box says up front what it will hold, and the language holds you to your word.

ideas.name: The overflow cliff
ideas.kid: A C++ int has walls. March past two billion and the number wraps round and lies to you.

ideas.name: Two costumes, one plan
ideas.kid: The same plan works in any language. The algorithm is the thing, the language is the costume it wears.

ideas.name: The mirage
ideas.kid: Code that compiles, runs and is still wrong. Looking right is not being right, so check against truth, not looks.

ideas.name: The one-stroke rule
ideas.kid: A drawing that is all in one piece can be traced without lifting the pencil exactly when it has no odd corners, or exactly two.

ideas.name: A negative turns the tables
ideas.kid: Multiplying both sides by a negative turns the whole number line around, so the sign between them has to turn with it

ideas.name: The speed gap
ideas.kid: A plan translated in advance runs far faster than one translated as it goes; do not believe the number, time it yourself

ideas.name: Route and weather
ideas.kid: After a hard morning you report the route you took and the weather you met, never a score; the story is the data that improves the next one

ideas.name: Look at the extreme
ideas.kid: Question the biggest, the smallest, the nearest or the first thing in the problem, because the extreme one has nowhere to hide

ideas.name: Race pace
ideas.kid: Read every story first, then spend your minutes where they buy the most; the reading is not time taken from solving

ideas.name: Same grader, same rules
ideas.kid: The grader does not know your age, your language or your story. It reads a file and a clock, and that is exactly why its yes means something

ideas.name: A reason beside every step
ideas.kid: In geometry the answer is only half the work; the other half is the reason written next to it

ideas.name: Distance is a triangle
ideas.kid: Any straight-line distance on a map is the long side of a right triangle you can build out of the across and the up

ideas.name: Powers of ten are a zoom lever
ideas.kid: Scientific notation is the universe's zoom lever: slide it up for stars, slide it down for dust, and every notch is one more ten

ideas.name: The protocol card
ideas.kid: Before a hard thing, the tired version of you needs a card from the calm version of you; write it while you are calm, and write it yourself

ideas.name: Park it and come back
ideas.kid: A stuck problem gets parked, not fought; fresh eyes are a real tool and the only thing they cost you is pride

ideas.name: Count the scarce ingredient
ideas.kid: Zeros on the end come from tens, tens come from twos meeting fives, and the fives run out first, so count the scarce one

ideas.name: Which middle tells the truth
ideas.kid: Mean, median and mode are three different stories about one pile of numbers, and every one of them can lie; knowing which one lies when is the actual skill

ideas.name: Data has holes
ideas.kid: Real logs have gaps in them, and an honest log says where its holes are instead of papering over them

ideas.name: The smallest criminal
ideas.kid: If a claim ever fails there is a smallest failure; arrest that one, squeeze a smaller accomplice out of it, and the crime never happened at all

ideas.name: Set the problem
ideas.kid: You own an idea completely only when you can build a problem that teaches it to somebody else

ideas.name: Edge cases are ambush points
ideas.kid: Strong test data waits where plans like to break: the smallest case, the biggest case and the tie

ideas.name: Plant it early, pay it off late
ideas.kid: A good talk hides a seed early and harvests it at the end, and the room feels it coming without knowing why

ideas.name: Some numbers escape every fraction
ideas.kid: Root 2 slips through every fraction there is, and you can prove that no fraction will ever catch it

ideas.name: Read code like a book
ideas.kid: Strong programmers read far more code than they write, and annotating somebody else's clean solution is training rather than copying

ideas.name: Rest is training
ideas.kid: Before a long climb you do less, not more; the day's learning finishes while you are asleep, so the resting is part of the work

ideas.name: Weigh the information
ideas.kid: A question is only worth asking if every possible answer teaches you something, so the best weighing splits the possibilities as evenly as it can

ideas.name: Subtract the inside
ideas.kid: To measure a border, take the inside away from the whole

ideas.name: The state map
ideas.kid: Draw every amount as a dot and every move as a line, then hunt the shortest path

ideas.name: Share the factor
ideas.kid: When two multiplications share the same number, pull it out front and subtract or add the rest first, instead of multiplying twice.

ideas.name: Count the overlap once
ideas.kid: When two groups share some members, add the groups then subtract the shared part once, or you count it twice.

ideas.name: Pair the ends
ideas.kid: Add the first and last number, then the second and second-last, every pair gives the same total, so multiply that pair-total by half the count.

ideas.name: Layer by layer
ideas.kid: Find everyone one hop away first, then everyone one hop past them

ideas.name: Two colors or a cycle
ideas.kid: Alternate two colors around a loop; an odd loop always clashes, so it needs a third

ideas.name: Two facts, two unknowns
ideas.kid: One equation cannot pin down two mystery numbers. Get a second true fact about them, then use both together to trap just one.

ideas.name: Current is a flow
ideas.kid: Current is charge flowing, like water flowing through a pipe

ideas.name: Narrow the pipe
ideas.kid: A resistor is a narrow pipe that slows the flow down

ideas.name: Ask the world
ideas.kid: A sensor asks the world one question and waits for the answer

ideas.name: Time the bounce
ideas.kid: Sound bounces off things, so timing the bounce tells you how far

ideas.name: Bright bounces, dark soaks
ideas.kid: Bright things bounce light back, dark things soak it up

ideas.name: Current into a push
ideas.kid: A motor turns electric current into a turning push

ideas.name: Trade speed for strength
ideas.kid: Gears trade speed for strength, slower turn, stronger push

ideas.name: Pressure that fades
ideas.kid: A battery pushes current like pressure, and the pressure fades with use

ideas.name: Persistence of vision
ideas.kid: A blinking light looks steady when it blinks faster than your eyes can follow

ideas.name: Pitch is a wiggle rate
ideas.kid: A note is a wiggle, and a faster wiggle sounds higher

ideas.name: Long strings, low notes
ideas.kid: A longer or heavier string wiggles slower, so it sounds lower

ideas.name: A lever trades distance for force
ideas.kid: A longer effort arm needs less force to lift the same load, but it moves further

ideas.name: Friction resists sliding
ideas.kid: Friction depends on the surfaces touching and how hard they press, not on how big the patch looks

ideas.name: Tolerance
ideas.kid: A printed part is never exactly the drawn size, and the gap between them is called tolerance

ideas.name: Infill trades time for strength
ideas.kid: More plastic inside a print takes longer to make but holds more weight before it fails

ideas.name: The triangle locks the shape
ideas.kid: A triangle cannot lean without a side changing length, so it holds its shape when a square will not

ideas.name: A small signal flips a big switch
ideas.kid: A driver lets a tiny signal turn a much bigger current on and off without carrying it itself

ideas.name: Equal radius, equal distance
ideas.kid: A compass keeps one radius fixed, so every point where two same-sized circles cross sits that exact same distance from both centers.

ideas.name: Some sums have more ways
ideas.kid: Two dice can land on the same sum in more than one way; count the ways to make each sum before you compare their chances.

ideas.name: Same shape, moved
ideas.kid: Slide, turn or flip a shape and every length and angle stays the same; only where it sits changes.

ideas.name: Scale keeps the shape
ideas.kid: A scaled copy keeps every angle the same and multiplies every side by the same number; find that one number first.

ideas.name: A polygon is triangles fanned out
ideas.kid: Draw every diagonal from one corner of a polygon and it splits into triangles; the corners add up to that many times 180.

ideas.name: Pi is the wheel's own number
ideas.kid: Roll a circle once around and divide the distance by how wide it is; you always land near the same number, pi.

ideas.name: Expected value is the average payout
ideas.kid: Multiply each outcome by its chance and add them up; that average payout says whether a game is fair.

ideas.name: Midpoint is the average
ideas.kid: A segment's midpoint is just the average of the two x's and the average of the two y's.

ideas.name: Choose without order
ideas.kid: Choosing a group does not care about order; Pascal's triangle counts how many groups of each size you can choose.

ideas.name: Condition shrinks the whole
ideas.kid: Given information shrinks the whole you are counting against; only count inside the row or column you were told is true.

ideas.name: Parallel lines copy the angle
ideas.kid: A line crossing two parallel lines copies the same angle to matching corners and swaps it at alternate corners.

ideas.name: Cubic units are not square units
ideas.kid: Area is measured in flat squares and volume in solid cubes; keep the unit's own shape in the label or the number lies.

ideas.name: Give the smallest chain
ideas.kid: When you must give away boxes, give the shortest chain so the least is lost.

ideas.name: Someone must win
ideas.kid: On this board a draw is impossible, one side always connects.

ideas.name: Falling and missing
ideas.kid: An orbit is a fall that keeps missing the ground because it moves sideways fast enough.

ideas.name: Commutator undo
ideas.kid: A short move sequence and its exact opposite can swap a few pieces and leave the rest alone.

ideas.name: Hanging piece
ideas.kid: A piece nobody defends is free to take.

ideas.name: Back rank mate
ideas.kid: A king boxed in by its own pawns can be mated along the open back row.

ideas.name: Fork
ideas.kid: One piece jumps to a square where it attacks two enemy pieces at once.

ideas.name: Pin
ideas.kid: A piece cannot move without leaving its own king in check.

ideas.name: King-assisted mate
ideas.kid: Your own king guards the square your mating piece lands on.

ideas.name: Stalemate trap
ideas.kid: No legal move is only a draw if the king is not also in check.

ideas.name: Skewer
ideas.kid: A check forces a piece to move, and a bigger piece behind it falls.

ideas.name: Smothered mate
ideas.kid: A king's own pieces block every escape, and a knight delivers mate.

ideas.name: Defended mate
ideas.kid: The mating piece is guarded, so the king cannot capture it.

ideas.name: The power budget
ideas.kid: A battery's milliamp-hour rating divided by how many milliamps something draws predicts how many hours it lasts.

ideas.name: A schematic is not the board
ideas.kid: A schematic shows what connects to what; a layout also decides where, and where changes how long the wires have to be.

ideas.name: Pressure becomes thrust
ideas.kid: Squeezed air pushes water out fast, and the escaping water pushes the rocket the other way.

ideas.name: Nose heavy flies straight
ideas.kid: A rocket flies straight when its centre of mass sits ahead of its centre of pressure, and fins move the centre of pressure back.

ideas.name: Orbit is falling and missing
ideas.kid: An orbit is falling toward a planet while moving sideways fast enough to keep missing it.

ideas.name: Pulse width sets the angle
ideas.kid: A hobby servo reads how wide a repeating pulse is and turns to match it, one width for each end of its travel.

ideas.name: The loop has a cost
ideas.kid: A microcontroller repeats its loop forever, and every line inside it takes real time, so a slow loop can miss a fast event.

ideas.name: Signal fades with obstacles
ideas.kid: A radio signal weakens with distance, and loses even more strength passing through walls than through open air.

ideas.name: Light time limits control
ideas.kid: A radio command takes real time to travel, so a signal to Mars can take minutes each way and you cannot drive it live.

ideas.name: Thermal mass and insulation
ideas.kid: Insulation does not stop heat leaving, it slows the rate, so a wrapped object stays warm longer than a bare one.

ideas.name: Tilt cuts the light
ideas.kid: A tilted solar panel catches less sunlight per area than one facing the sun straight on.

ideas.name: Transistors add up to gates
ideas.kid: A logic gate is built from a handful of transistors wired to switch each other, and a chip with many gates has many more inside.

ideas.name: A signal takes time through a gate
ideas.kid: Even a fast logic gate takes a small delay to respond, and that delay adds up when many gates are chained together.

ideas.name: Flux clears the oxide
ideas.kid: Flux is the acid that eats away the oxide so solder can grip bare metal

ideas.name: Plastic remembers its heat
ideas.kid: PLA turns rubbery once it warms past its glass transition, then stiffens again as it cools

ideas.name: Leaves catch photons
ideas.kid: A leaf uses the same light your sensor reads to build sugar out of air and water

ideas.name: Time the radio bounce
ideas.kid: A satellite times how late its own radio signal arrives to say where you are

ideas.name: Nerves carry a signal
ideas.kid: A nerve signal is fast but not instant, and most of a reaction is your brain deciding

ideas.name: Falling around the earth
ideas.kid: A satellite never stops falling, it just moves fast enough to keep missing the ground

ideas.name: The globe is a grid
ideas.kid: Latitude and longitude wrap a flat grid around a sphere, so one direction changes size

ideas.name: Echo timing in a living sonar
ideas.kid: A bat finds distance by timing its own echo, the same trick as an ultrasonic sensor

ideas.name: Air gets thin with height
ideas.kid: Air pressure drops the higher you climb, because less air is stacked above you

ideas.name: A battery runs out of reaction
ideas.kid: A battery stores a chemical reaction, and its voltage sags once that reaction runs low

ideas.name: Heat fades the ink
ideas.kid: Thermal paper has no ink at all, just a dye that turns black when it gets hot

ideas.name: Dry air cannot hold heat
ideas.kid: Places with little water vapour in the air swing far between a hot day and a cold night

ideas.name: The tilt makes the season
ideas.kid: Earth's 23.4 degree tilt, not its distance from the sun, is why seasons happen

ideas.name: Rust is a slow fire
ideas.kid: Rust is iron combining with oxygen, the same reaction as burning, just far slower

ideas.name: One-way valves keep flow forward
ideas.kid: A valve lets flow go one way and blocks it the other, just like a diode

ideas.name: Muscles only pull
ideas.kid: A muscle can only contract, so bending a joint both ways needs two muscles in a pair

ideas.name: Light has a speed limit
ideas.kid: Nothing travels faster than light, so a distant signal always arrives minutes late

ideas.name: A square turn is 90 degrees
ideas.kid: Turn four times by 90 degrees and you are facing the way you started

ideas.name: The pupil is a sensor too
ideas.kid: Your eye's pupil grows and shrinks to control how much light gets in

ideas.name: Your brain recognizes fast
ideas.kid: Special brain cells spot a face in a fraction of a second

ideas.name: A full turn is the whole globe
ideas.kid: 360 degrees takes you all the way around a circle or all the way around the Earth

ideas.name: Overtones give a note its colour
ideas.kid: A note is not one wiggle, it is a stack of wiggles, and the mix gives an instrument its own colour

ideas.name: Beats between close notes
ideas.kid: Two notes almost the same pitch wobble together, and the wobbles per second equal how far apart they are

ideas.name: Simple ratios sound sweet
ideas.kid: Notes whose wiggle rates make a simple ratio like 3 to 2 sound settled together

ideas.name: Resonance: things sing along
ideas.kid: A string can start vibrating on its own when the right note reaches it, without being struck

ideas.name: A motor brakes its own current
ideas.kid: A spinning motor pushes back against its own current; stop it and that push disappears, so current jumps up.

ideas.name: Thrust must beat weight
ideas.kid: An aircraft only leaves the ground once its motors' combined thrust is bigger than its own weight.

ideas.name: Matched motors still differ
ideas.kid: Two motors from the same batch still differ slightly in friction and winding, so equal power never means equal speed.

ideas.name: Correct by how far off you are
ideas.kid: A proportional controller pushes harder the further off it is, and eases off as the gap closes.

ideas.name: The loop outraces the fall
ideas.kid: A flight controller checks and corrects a quad's tilt hundreds of times a second, faster than gravity can tip it over.

ideas.name: Dead reckoning drifts
ideas.kid: Flying or driving by estimated motion alone stacks small errors together, so the machine drifts further from the truth the longer it goes.

ideas.name: Torque fades with reach
ideas.kid: A servo's twisting force can lift less weight the farther out from its shaft that weight sits.

ideas.name: Stay inside the support triangle
ideas.kid: A body stays balanced only while its centre of mass sits above the shape drawn by the feet touching the ground.

ideas.name: Place value
ideas.kid: Where a digit sits decides what it is worth

ideas.name: Line up the places
ideas.kid: Line up the ones, the tens and the hundreds, then add or subtract

ideas.name: Know your facts
ideas.kid: Know your times tables so you never have to count

ideas.name: Break it into parts
ideas.kid: Multiply the parts and add them back together

ideas.name: Share it out
ideas.kid: Share the number out one place at a time

ideas.name: What is left over
ideas.kid: What is left over still means something

ideas.name: Factors and multiples
ideas.kid: Factors divide it evenly, multiples come from multiplying it

ideas.name: Break it into primes
